items.title: tigerless-labs/agent-memory
items.excerpt: Long-term memory runtime for AI agents — plain Markdown as the source of truth, local ranked retrieval, and an independent sleep-time Manage layer. Claude Code and Codex share one store. No API key.
items.summary: Agent-memory provides long-term memory runtime for AI agents using plain Markdown as source of truth, local ranked retrieval, independent sleep-time layer. Works with Claude Code and Codex. Requires no API key.
items.usefulness: Could enable local agent memory persistence for Python tools without external dependencies or authentication overhead.
items.to_verify: Whether plain Markdown retrieval actually supports ranked search on large document sets and what the latency and accuracy constraints are.

items.title: Show HN: Foremerge – Catch intent conflicts between parallel coding agents
items.excerpt: At, GPTree, we run several coding agents across our team on one repo using parallel worktrees. Apart from wasted time reviewing and fixing conflicts at PR time, the failures that hurt the most are when multiple plans or tickets cause architecture changes that cannot both be true. Ex. one agent replaces a class while another one is in the process of extending it. Git only notices if the resulting patches happen to touch the same lines and the review only catches it if they are familiar with both tickets. items.summary: Foremerge detects intent conflicts between parallel coding agents using worktrees on one repo—catches architecture collisions git and PR review miss, like one agent replacing a class while another extends it.
items.usefulness: Could inform multi-agent Python tool coordination by showing how to detect semantic conflicts before merge, not just line-level diffs.
items.to_verify: Whether Foremerge's intent detection works without domain-specific rules and how it scales to complex architectural changes across agents.
